= RTDB scoped schema-name parsing

This directory preserves Apache Avro Rust 0.21.0 from the published source archive.
link:UPSTREAM.json[The upstream manifest] records the archive SHA256 and every original file's SHA256.
The source archive SHA256 is 36fa98bc79671c7981272d91a8753a928ff6a1cd8e4f20a44c45bd5d313840bf.
Original license and notice files, fixtures, examples, source tests, and their assertions are retained.
Only Cargo.toml and src/schema.rs modify original files; the scoped policy module and its regression sources are additions.

Kafka depends directly on this path at the same pinned version.
There is no workspace-wide registry patch.
Its production Avro parsing still calls the original parse_str_with_list API and therefore retains the original global validator behavior.
The root Cargo.lock changes only this package's source identity, removing the registry source and archive checksum while preserving its dependency list.
No dependency resolution or Cargo command was executed during the adaptation.

== Scoped policy

Schema::parse_str_with_list_with_name_policy adds a synchronous parser-local policy.
The policy is a passive borrowed object for name construction, field and enum validation, record-field lookup rules, and an optional second reference candidate.
The Parser remains a passive single-writer call-local transient, owning its existing schema maps and parse order.
Its new optional reference is borrowed only for the parse call and never escapes into returned schema values.
Name, Alias, and Schema remain passive immutable values with their existing shapes.
No global validator registration, thread-local setting, lock, task, background state, or mutable process cache is introduced.

Every dynamic root/reference declaration, type alias, reference candidate, field, enum symbol, and nested type-name hint in the scoped path uses the supplied policy.
Names and validation results must be stable for the same inputs and construction context during a call; policy callbacks may reenter parsing.
Object-valued type wrappers use the inner declaration name and namespace selected by ordinary parsing, retaining one effective definition key through input indexing, parsing, and ordered output.
Duplicate policy-resolved input names return NameCollision, including global names normalized from None and explicit empty namespaces.
The returned tuple contains the root and a vector of referenced schemas in input iterator order.
Parsed record, enum, and fixed aliases produce references to the canonical definition name.
Scoped fixed logical conversion updates both the canonical entry and its aliases to the final duration, UUID, or fixed-decimal schema, including nested definitions.
As in the original parser, aliases of unparsed external definitions are not preindexed.
References to those forward aliases may therefore fail before their declaring input has been parsed.
That retained limitation requires a separate production behavior decision before activating Java name policies.
The existing unscoped constructors and parser routes retain their global hooks, panic/error boundaries, and diagnostics.
A scoped policy can return false from record_field_lookup_uses_aliases to index only raw field names.
The default is true, preserving ordinary and existing scoped alias lookup and duplicate-name behavior.
Opting out allows a field alias to match another field's raw name without replacing that field's index or treating a later raw name as a duplicate.
Aliases remain on RecordField for schema resolution; only the existing lookup index changes its membership.
Kafka's JavaNames policy has not opted out in this prerequisite, and production parsing remains unchanged.
A scoped policy must return a name whose namespace has already been resolved against its construction context.
The parser normalizes a returned None namespace to Some("").
This explicit empty namespace is retained by Name::fully_qualified_name and gives global definitions, aliases, and references the same Eq/Hash key.
Name::fullname ignores an empty namespace even when a default namespace is supplied.
Definitions retaining a Name (records, enums, ordinary fixed, and fixed decimal) serialize namespace:"" explicitly; ordinary reference serialization continues to emit the fullname and reparsing follows the caller's policy candidate rules.
Fixed definitions converted to Uuid or Duration discard their original name and namespace.

The qualification audit covers parser fetch and alias registration, schema resolution helpers, default-value validation in types.rs, and later encoder/decoder reference qualification.
All of those retain an already present empty namespace instead of applying their enclosing-namespace fallback.
No absolute-name boolean is added to Name.
The internal ASCII duration name is created only by serialization, while dynamic duration declarations go through the policy before conversion to Schema::Duration.
Scoped default-error diagnostics use Debug schema descriptions rather than invoking a serializer that could consult that global duration-name constructor.
The unscoped path retains canonical-form descriptions.
Debug schema descriptions use existing structural Debug implementations and do not serialize or construct names.

== Allocation and verification

The policy adds one borrowed fat pointer to the call-local Parser and no additional retained collection or output owner.
Normalizing None to an empty String allocates no string payload.
The second reference candidate is constructed only after the primary is absent from parsed, resolving, and input schema maps.
Its one Name value uses the policy's ordinary owned name/namespace strings and drops with that lookup.
Existing parser collections and returned schemas retain their original ownership.
Final logical registration replaces entries in the existing parsed-schema map; temporary owned names and alias vectors remain bounded by the declaration already being parsed.
Logical references clone the final logical schema, as the upstream helper already does when parsing an external logical definition on demand.
A policy is responsible for its own allocations; the future Kafka Java policy and conversion admission are separate work.

Thirteen new unit regressions and one isolated integration regression cover initialized global defaults, globals that reject every name, fields, enum symbols, fixed/record declarations, named and field alias distinctions, cyclic and external references, nested unions, explicit empty namespaces, hash/qualification identity, serialization/reparse, candidate precedence, nested policies, policy errors, wrapper identity and input order, normalized duplicate names, canonical alias resolution, and nested/external fixed logical types.
Resolver and value-resolution assertions check returned canonical reference identities against actual definitions.
Four additional regression sources compare raw-only lookup with ordinary and default scoped parsing for both alias/raw collision directions, shared aliases, retained alias metadata, duplicate raw names and reader-field alias compatibility.
The isolated integration target owns its rejecting global validators without changing another target's globals.
All original schema.rs test bodies and the complete original validator.rs remain byte-identical to the archive.
Compilation, tests, formatters, and runtime discovery remain unexecuted under the Phase1 work order.
This adaptation does not enable Unicode schema names in Kafka production or close its Connect scrubbing and allocation obligations.
